Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: ABS is zero-marked in the singular (bare stem); plural -t is not a dedicated ABS marker (shared with common plural). No overt ABS case marker. Original annotation of 1 was incorrect.
curated_comment: Kalaallisut/West Greenlandic (kala1399, ISO kal, Eskimo-Aleut) is a consistently ergative language per Sadock (2003) and Fortescue (1984). ERG/relative suffix -(u)p (sg.) / -it (pl.) marks transitive subjects and possessors uniformly across tense, aspect, mood, animacy, and clause type. Three corrections from the original xlsx: GB409_1 (1→0: ABS is zero-marked), GB409_2 (1→0: 1st person pronouns use a single direct-case form), GB409_3 (1→0: same for 2nd person). GB409_14 was empty and filled in as 1 (Sadock §9.2.1.6). Seven '?' values resolved: GB409_9=1, GB409_15=1, GB409_17=1, GB409_19=1, GB409_21=1, GB409_22=0 (no additional conditioning), GB409_23=1 (ERG=GEN: possessors take -(u)p). Glottocode kala1399 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: 1st and 2nd person pronouns have a single 'direct case' (DIR) form for all grammatical roles (Sadock §2.11.1.2: 'The first and second person pronouns have only one form for all the direct cases'). No distinct ERG form. Corrected from 1 to 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Same as GB409_2: 2nd person pronouns use a single DIR form with no distinct ergative. Corrected from 1 to 0.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: No dedicated 3rd person pronouns; demonstratives serve as 3rd person and DO have distinct ERG forms (e.g., matuma = ERG singular of 'this'). Value 1 confirmed.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs take ERG/relative suffix -(u)p (singular) or -it (plural) as transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: ERG applies regardless of aspect; no aspect-based split documented in either source.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: ERG applies regardless of aspect; no aspect-based split documented.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: ERG marking not conditioned by tense; applies in all temporal contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: ERG marking applies in non-past (including future -ssa-) without conditioning.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: Indicative is the primary mood; ERG applies throughout.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: WG has 9 moods; ERG applies across all of them including conjunctive and participial subordinate moods (Fortescue §1.7-1.9).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: All declarative/realis contexts show ERG alignment.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: In future/optative (irrealis-like) contexts, ERG still marks transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: Sadock §9.2.1.6: 'the ergative marks the more agentive term of transitives.' Value filled in from empty cell.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Fortescue §2.1.1.2.2: 'no distinction between agentive/non-agentive.' Even non-agentive subjects of derived transitives retain ERG marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: Topicality does not condition case marking (Fortescue §1.12: WG is not topic-prominent).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: Same: topicality does not condition case marking; non-topical A also takes ERG.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate transitive subjects consistently take ERG (Fortescue §2.1.1.2.2).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Animacy does not condition ERG marking; inanimate transitive subjects also take -(u)p.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: ERG applies in main clauses throughout.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: In subordinate clauses (conjunctive, participial, dependent moods), nominal transitive subjects retain ERG -(u)p.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Source_comment: Sadock 2003: in passim; Fortescue 1984: in passim
Comment: No additional conditioning beyond the core transitive subject function. Person-based split (GB409_2=0, GB409_3=0) is already captured in earlier features.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Possessor phrases take the same ERG/relative case -(u)p (Sadock §5.5.3.1; Fortescue §2.1.1.4.6). Explicit ERG=GEN syncretism.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Instrumental = -mik (Fortescue §2.1.1.4.3), distinct from ERG -(u)p. Comitative expressed derivationally. No ERG=INST/COM syncretism.
